Comment: CloudLab c240g5: the three kinds of dataset update (U14) on Wikipedia c1024, 4 data nodes and 4 spares (the full rebuild's), the load constant at 560 q/s (0.6 x C4 938, as 4to8). Four minor batches of the 2026-02 diff (b4x5: 775K inserts, 5% of the base, and about 744K deletes each), 400 s apart; a major epoch after the second (lists longer than 400 split, the longest first, and shorter than 5 merge, at most 1300 lists: about the base's 99.9th percentile of 358 and its shortest 0.35%; the cap keeps the graph patch in its one 268 MB frame, at about 190 KB a split); a full rebuild after the fourth, to the next generation of the data the four make (results/wiki-updates-2026-11-22/build-next-generation.sh: fusion_build --from-index, GP, rtier_segment). Every entry runs to its end before the next starts. The inserts take IDs and locations from 15,513,418 (Headroom 1.25 leaves room for 18,616,102), and the next generation's lists must fit ListHeadroom 2.0 (5,888). Answers are scored per data version (scripts/score_answers.py) against <GroundTruth>.versions/, made on CloudLab on 2026-11-22 (results/gt-versions-2026-11-22). UpdateLease 60m and StageTimeout 60m (the defaults, 10m and 30m, would give up a batch or a major epoch that holds the cluster longer: the controller's lease is a safety timeout for a dead update controller, StageTimeout bounds each rtier-updater run (-timeout); neither is a pace). Timing from the calibration run (experiment.wiki-c1024-cloudlab-gpu-updates-probe.json, 2026-11-22, inserts routed side by side): batch 1 took 271 s (218 s to decide, nearly all of it routing 775,671 inserts on half of node0's CPUs; 53 s from the staging to the reclaim), and the major epoch after it 30 s (878 splits and 434 merges of the lists the batch changed, a 166 MB graph patch), so a batch with its major epoch (about 305 s) leaves 95-130 s of load with no update running before the next entry: 400 s apart (2026-11-22), where 330 s left 25-60 s. The rebuild comes at 1720 s and gets 680 s before the load ends (its time is not measured yet), so the load runs 2400 s.
